s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological deficit with speech disturbance and hemiparesis
key_facts: Early ischemic changes in the left insula and frontal lobe on noncontrast head CT
Acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery at M1/M2
Chronic occlusion of the left internal carotid artery
Mild pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid analysis

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery at M1/M2 and early ischemic changes in the left insula and frontal lobe on noncontrast head CT

shortlist.label: Stroke due to atrial fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has persistent atrial fibrillation and acute speech disturbance with right-sided weakness

shortlist.label: Cardioembolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has atrial fibrillation and evidence of emboli in segmental arteries of the right lower lobe

shortlist.label: Cerebral vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated C-reactive protein and mild pleocytosis in cerebrospinal fluid analysis

shortlist.label: Takayasu arteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic occlusion of the left internal carotid artery and presence of systemic symptoms such as elevated C-reactive protein

raw.rationale: The patient's persistent atrial fibrillation, acute speech disturbance, right-sided weakness, and imaging findings of early ischemic changes and acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery are consistent with a cardioembolic stroke, which is a type of ischemic stroke caused by an embolus originating from the heart.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: Too broad, as cardioembolic stroke is a specific subtype of ischemic stroke

rejected.label: Stroke due to atrial fibrillation
rejected.why: Essentially synonymous with cardioembolic stroke in this context, but less specific

rejected.label: Cerebral vasculitis
rejected.why: Not supported by the presence of atrial fibrillation and the pattern of ischemic changes

rejected.label: Takayasu arteritis
rejected.why: Not suggested by the patient's age, clinical presentation, or imaging findings

gold: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
